mathgap.title: Direct count assignment at point of mention
mathgap.principle: When a statement directly gives a count for a person, set that person's current count to the given number at that point in the narrative.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a sentence states "X has N onions" (or a similar phrasing).
mathgap.example: Treating "X has N onions" as a hint that X's final count is N, ignoring later transfers that change X's count.

mathgap.title: Directionality of more/fewer statements
mathgap.principle: Interpret "X has N more than Y" as X = Y + N, and "X has N fewer than Y" as X = Y - N.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a sentence contains a comparative phrase with a numeric offset.
mathgap.example: Interpreting "X has N more than Y" as Y = X + N, swapping the direction of the relationship.

mathgap.title: Split‑all handling
mathgap.principle: When a person splits all of their items equally among two recipients, each recipient receives half of the original amount.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement says "X splits all their onions between Y and Z".
mathgap.example: Giving each recipient the full amount instead of half when splitting.

mathgap.title: Sequential transfer handling with updated counts
mathgap.principle: Process each transfer in the order it appears: subtract the transferred amount from the giver's current count and add it to the receiver's current count.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When encountering a "X gives N onions to Y" statement.
mathgap.example: Applying a later transfer before an earlier one, or using pre‑transfer counts for a later transfer.

mathgap.title: Substitution of known signed differences into signed difference equalities
mathgap.principle: If a signed difference (e.g., X‑Y) is already known numerically, substitute its value into any equality that contains that signed difference.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When solving an equation of the form (X‑Y) = (A‑B) and one side has been previously determined.
mathgap.example: Leaving (X‑Y) as a variable even though its value was already computed earlier.

mathgap.title: Chronological evaluation of statements
mathgap.principle: Read and apply statements in the exact order they appear, because later statements refer to counts as they stand after earlier statements.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Throughout the problem, especially when transfers and relational statements are interleaved.
mathgap.example: Using a person's initial count for a relational statement that appears after a transfer that changed that count.

mathgap.title: Conditional transfer handling
mathgap.principle: For a clause "If X has more than N items, X will transfer their items to Y", evaluate the condition using the current count of X and apply the transfer only if the condition holds.
mathgap.example: Always performing the transfer regardless of whether X's count exceeds N.

mathgap.title: Target variable dependency analysis
mathgap.principle: Trace which equations and variables directly or indirectly affect the target variable, and ignore statements that do not influence it.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When the problem contains many irrelevant statements.
mathgap.example: Attempting to solve the entire system of equations even though most variables are unrelated to the target.

mathgap.title: Signed difference handling with trivial equality detection
mathgap.principle: If a signed‑difference equality has identical expressions on both sides (e.g., (X‑Y) = (X‑Y)), recognize it as a trivial identity and discard it.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When encountering equations that simplify to a tautology.
mathgap.example: Treating a trivial equality as providing new information and using it to solve for variables.

mathgap.title: Signed difference equality parsing
mathgap.principle: When a statement says "The number of onions that X has more than Y is equal to the difference between the number of onions that A and B have", interpret it as the signed difference equation (X - Y) = (A - B), preserving the order of terms.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a comparative phrase appears inside a "the number of ..." construction without an explicit numeric offset.
mathgap.example: Interpreting the statement as X = Y + (A - B) or as |X - Y| = |A - B| instead of (X - Y) = (A - B).

mathgap.description: Treating signed difference statements as absolute differences or swapping term order
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model confuses the directionality of signed differences and often replaces (X‑Y) with |X‑Y| or flips the sides, losing sign information.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Always keep the order of terms as written and treat the expression as a signed difference, not an absolute value.

mathgap.why_it_happens: The model applies all transfers after parsing the whole text, forgetting that later statements depend on earlier updates.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Process each transfer immediately when it appears, updating the giver's and receiver's counts before handling subsequent statements.

mathgap.description: Assuming explicit counts are final after all transfers
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model treats a direct count as a permanent value, overlooking later transfers that modify that count.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Treat direct count statements as setting the current count at that point; later transfers can change it.

mathgap.why_it_happens: The model applies transfers unconditionally, missing the need to evaluate the condition first.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Check the condition on the giver's current count before performing a conditional transfer.

mathgap.description: Misinterpreting multiplicative increase statements as additive
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model reads "increases by K times" as "adds K" instead of multiplying.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: When a statement mentions a multiplicative increase, multiply the current count by the given factor.
